key_insight: MC-EvoBench introduces a controlled way to test whether Minecraft agents truly learn reusable skills from experience, rather than just carrying over memories, resources, or lucky outcomes. It focuses on measuring genuine capability growth across tasks and worlds.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of evaluating recursive self-improvement in embodied agents: distinguishing real skill acquisition from superficial performance gains caused by saved state, unequal task exposure, or early execution failures.
method: Build MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft evaluation benchmark designed to isolate experience-driven improvement.
Compare agent behavior across repeated and later tasks to determine whether gains transfer beyond the original world or context.
Separate capability change from confounders such as carried-over resources, prior exposure differences, and failures that happen before learning can occur.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers a more reliable way to audit whether agents are actually improving through experience. For AI/ML practitioners working on embodied agents, it helps prevent misleading conclusions from evaluations that overstate learning.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing experience -> memory/capability -> transfer to new tasks
A comparison chart contrasting true skill gain vs. resource carryover vs. lucky success
An annotated Minecraft world/task sequence illustrating benchmark episodes
An icon set for memory, tools/resources, task success, and transfer learning
paper_title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
paper_authors: Jingwei Song, Zhisheng Chen, Bingfan Zeng, Jing Tang, Yubo Hou
